title: 32.4 A Dual-LC-Resonant Isolated DC-DC Converter Achieving 65.4% Peak Efficiency and Inherent Backscattering
problem: Integrated isolated DC-DC converters (with on-chip transformers) suffer from low peak efficiency (~52%) due to TX LC-oscillator losses, RX full-bridge rectifier losses, and parasitic transformer elements. Traditional feedback from RX to TX requires costly digital isolators; alternative RX-only regulation approaches sacrifice efficiency (<37%).
motivation: Harsh industrial environments demand galvanically isolated power delivery with high integration and efficiency; eliminating discrete transformers/components requires on-chip isolation but existing designs trade efficiency for integration.
method: The circuit uses two LC resonators (coil-capacitor circuits tuned to vibrate at a set frequency), optimized separately for the input and output sides. The input side drives oscillation through an optimized LC circuit, while the output side converts this to DC power using resonant rectification—a rectifier tuned to that frequency—instead of a traditional full-bridge rectifier that wastes energy across multiple diodes. The output side provides voltage regulation by modulating how much current it draws, which modulates the input resonator through backscattering (a technique where load changes couple back through the resonator), eliminating the need for an expensive digital isolator.
key_novelty: The dual-LC-resonant topology with inherent backscatter feedback achieves 65.4% peak efficiency and eliminates the need for digital isolators—a 6–13% efficiency gain compared to conventional isolated DC-DC converters.
contributions: Optimized dual-LC resonator design (TX and RX independent tuning) reduces oscillator and rectifier losses
Resonant rectification improves RX efficiency vs. full-bridge topology
Inherent backscatter feedback from RX to TX eliminates digital isolator cost/complexity
65.4% peak efficiency, largest reported gain vs. prior isolated converters
baselines: State-of-the-art integrated isolated converters (~52% peak efficiency)
limitations: Efficiency at light load, output regulation accuracy, and practical transformer parasitic modeling not discussed.
primary_theme: Dual-LC resonant isolated DC-DC with backscatter
